claims.text: A coherent interfacial layer forming an ordered L12-like phase will shift HEA multilayer creep from diffusion-dominated to dislocation-mediated deformation.
The as-deposited HEA multilayer may have partially incoherent interfaces.
AlCoCrFeNi2.1 is a eutectic high-entropy alloy.
AlCoCrFeNi2.1 is an L12-phase-forming composition.
A thin AlCoCrFeNi2.1-derived interfacial layer will promote coherency with adjacent HEA multilayer layers.
Diffusion-mediated creep is more dominant at higher temperatures in the proposed HEA multilayers.
Dislocation-mediated creep becomes more significant as temperature decreases in the proposed HEA multilayers.
An ordered L12-like interfacial phase minimizes lattice mismatch.
The coherent ordered interfacial phase acts as a barrier to homogeneous diffusion paths.
The coherent interlayer stabilizes the interface.
The coherent interlayer reduces stress concentrations by inhibiting rapid vacancy diffusion.
At high temperatures, the interlayer controls creep rate by impeding diffusive flow.
At lower temperatures, preserved interface coherency facilitates dislocation nucleation and motion.
Facilitated dislocation nucleation and motion promotes dislocation-mediated creep.
The engineered coherent interlayer will measurably shift the creep-mechanism transition temperature relative to unmodified multilayers.
The engineered coherent interlayer will lower creep rates through a controlled switch from diffusion creep toward dislocation creep.
Standard HEA multilayers without the engineered interlayer are predominantly diffusion-controlled at high temperatures and have a less distinct transition to dislocation creep.
The proposed benefit requires maintained interface coherency and may disappear if thickness, composition, or processing produces excessive misfit or incoherency.
The magnitude of the transition-temperature shift and creep-rate change remains undetermined.
A lack of statistically significant differences in activation energy, dislocation activity, and strain-rate behavior between modified and control multilayers would falsify the hypothesis.
